cases.about: 104 weeks of orders: trend plus season, eight weeks with a range, a 7% held-out error, two missing weeks named, one outlier left in and flagged.

call.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import csv
# parse weekly-orders.csv, fit trend + season, hold out 8, print rows
PY

call.title: Forecast — weekly-orders.csv, 8 weeks
call.content:
Forecast — weekly-orders.csv, 8 weeks
5,920 orders over the next 8 weeks (range 5,210–6,630), held-out error 7%

## Numbers
| Week of | Forecast | Low | High |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-09 | 705 | 640 | 770 |
| 2026-11-16 | 718 | 645 | 791 |
| 2026-11-23 | 760 | 680 | 840 |
| 2026-11-30 | 812 | 724 | 900 |
| 2026-12-07 | 790 | 696 | 884 |
| 2026-12-14 | 745 | 645 | 845 |
| 2026-12-21 | 690 | 584 | 796 |
| 2026-12-28 | 700 | 589 | 811 |
Total: 5,920 (5,210–6,630).

## Method
Trend plus week-of-year season: a straight line fitted to 104 weeks (2024-11-04 to 2026-11-02), plus the average lift of each week position across the two years. Fitted on the first 96 weeks and checked on the last 8, it was off by 7% on average. The range is ±1.5 standard deviations of the fit's errors, widening each week ahead.

## Assumptions
- Last year's late-November lift repeats; no price change or campaign the file cannot know about.
- 2 missing weeks (2025-12-29, 2026-01-05) were filled as missing, not as zero.
- The range is the spread the history supports, not a guarantee.

## Not measured
- 2025-08-18: 1,420 orders, 4 standard deviations above the fit; left in. Say if it should be excluded.

script.say:
5,920 orders over the next 8 weeks (5,210–6,630), trend plus season, held-out error 7%.

## Report
- read weekly-orders.csv (104 weeks); 1 command; wrote "Forecast — weekly-orders.csv, 8 weeks"
